blocking.section: Decision outcome (rules table, row Time); Confirmation
blocking.issue: The Time rule says wazero enforces limits.timeout as a plain per-call context deadline. The owning document requires that the call timer stop while the guest is parked in its one State Store call. A context deadline cannot be paused. In wazero, WithCloseOnContextDone starts a watcher goroutine per Call that closes the module when ctx.Done() fires, and the same ctx reaches Host Functions. If the rule is built as written with context.WithTimeout, a parked state.* call is killed at 5 ms and its instance is closed. During a State Store brownout (50 ms stateStoreTimeout in the owning document's Sizing table), every parked instance then becomes RZ-PLG-002 and is discarded. That produces the refill storm and fault-breaker trip the parked-bound design exists to prevent, and it contradicts the owning document's Default limits row.
blocking.evidence: ADR Time row: "`WithCloseOnContextDone(true)` with a per-call deadline from `limits.timeout`, default 5 ms (target)". Owning document, Default limits: "Wall-clock time per call (`limits.timeout`) | 5 ms (target) | Stopped while parked"; Runtime rule 7: "During its one State Store call the guest is parked, timer stopped".
blocking.fix: Reword the Time row to name a mechanism that can pause: "`WithCloseOnContextDone(true)` on a cancel-only per-call context (context.WithCancel of the request context); a host timer of `limits.timeout` cancels it, is stopped while the guest is parked in its State Store call and resumes with the remaining time; the State Store call uses its own `stateStoreTimeout` context (pack section 8.7)". Add a Confirmation limit case to the Plugin ABI conformance bullet: a parked `state_get` that lasts longer than `limits.timeout` returns to the guest without RZ-PLG-002, and the same guest then looping past the remaining time gets RZ-PLG-002.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (rules table, row Memory); Consequences
blocking.issue: The Memory row fixes only the page cap. It does not choose the linear-memory backing store, so the claim that Gateway limits.maxPluginMemoryBytes caps the Node cannot be shown to hold for process memory. With wazero defaults, linear memory is a Go-heap byte slice that grows by reallocation and copy. Each memory.grow briefly holds both the old and the new slice, and the old one stays as garbage until the next GC. Because this memory is live Go heap, it also raises the GOGC heap target: 2 GiB of Plugin memory can push the heap target to about 4 GiB under GOGC=100. Resident memory can therefore exceed the Node cap by up to 2x, which breaks the owning document's "Full reservation makes the Node cap a hard bound" rule and P6's "never crashes the Node" under a container memory limit. Research section 2.2 names the two wazero knobs that decide this (WithMemoryCapacityFromMax and experimental.MemoryAllocator), but the ADR mentions neither.
blocking.evidence: ADR Memory row: "`WithMemoryLimitPages` from `limits.memoryBytes`, default 16 MiB (target), replacing wazero's 65536-page (4 GiB) default ([source](https://github.com/wazero/wazero/blob/main/config.go)); Gateway `limits.maxPluginMemoryBytes` caps the Node". Research go-libraries-runtime.md section 2.2: "`WithMemoryCapacityFromMax(true)` allocates the maximum eagerly" and "`experimental.MemoryAllocator` lets the host supply the `LinearMemory` backing store".
blocking.fix: In the Memory row, choose and cite one backing store (research URLs config.go and experimental/memory.go). Either use `WithMemoryCapacityFromMax(true)`, which allocates eagerly, matches full reservation and avoids reallocation copies, or use an `experimental.MemoryAllocator` that reserves `limits.memoryBytes` outside the Go heap. State how the Node sets GOMEMLIMIT relative to maxPluginMemoryBytes. If the choice needs a benchmark first, add it to OQ-wasm-plugin-system-16 and add a Bad consequence for the resident-memory overhead (hypothesis). Add a Confirmation test: at the Node cap, with instances growing to their limit, resident memory stays within the cap plus the stated headroom (target).

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (rows Runtimes and cache, Compilation); Consequences
non_blocking.suggestion: In wazero main, a module's cache ID hashes the Wasm bytes, the listeners and the ensure-termination flag, not the memory limit (internal/wasm/module.go AssignModuleID). A shared NewCompilationCache engine keeps compiled modules reference-counted and frees them when the last CompiledModule.Close runs (internal/engine/wazevo/engine.go DeleteCompiledModule). As a result, "once per digest and memory limit" compiles native code only once per digest; the second runtime gets a cache hit. The 4 x Wasm bytes accounting per digest and limit is therefore conservative, and Retire can free code through Close. Add these files to the research (section 2.2) and use them to answer the "free one module early" part of OQ-wasm-plugin-system-16. Also state that Retire calls CompiledModule.Close so the refcount reaches zero, since the shared engine otherwise lives until Cache.Close.

wazero.NewRuntimeConfig() falls back silently to the interpreter where the compiler is unsupported, which would miss SM-6 by about 10x. Say that internal/pluginhost uses NewRuntimeConfigCompiler() and that ruralzd refuses to activate Plugins, reporting a degraded state, when the compiler is unavailable. Add this to the review checklist item.

"a Hot Reload that keeps a digest reuses its compiled code and pools" is too broad. The owning document shares a pool only for equal digest, canonical `config` and limits (Runtime rule 3). Reword to "reuses its compiled code, and its pools when `config` and limits are also unchanged".

WithCloseOnContextDone starts one watcher goroutine and one channel per Call (internal/wasm/module_instance.go). This is bounded by concurrent calls but is a fixed per-call cost inside the 50 us SM-6 budget. State that SM-6 includes it, beside the #2466 loop-check overhead that the Bad consequence already names.

Say how a `limits.memoryBytes` value that is not a multiple of 64 KiB maps to WithMemoryLimitPages: round down, or reject with the code proposed in OQ-wasm-plugin-system-9. Without that rule, Nodes and audit may compute N differently.
